subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` credential-shaped names bypass the generic sensitive-name block for that active skill's host run, and what isolation boundary prevents unrelated exec leakage?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible and affects documented behavior, but the repair intentionally moves credentials into executable subprocess environments and overlaps an inverse secret-leak concern.

options.title: Admit scoped active-skill env secrets
options.body: Permit only keys explicitly configured for the active skill to pass the sensitive-name check, keep dangerous host-env names blocked, and add tests for selected-skill delivery plus unrelated exec isolation.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive allowlist
options.body: Require skills to declare every credential-shaped env name in metadata and update docs or doctor guidance so arbitrary `skills.entries.*.env` credential names are not promised.

options.title: Defer to a new secret contract
options.body: Do not change the current sanitizer until maintainers define a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Admit scoped active-skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit only keys explicitly configured for the active skill to pass the sensitive-name check, keep dangerous host-env names blocked, and add tests for selected-skill delivery plus unrelated exec isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent merged history in the overlapping skill env and SecretRef runtime path.
